newsitem.title: USA: Senate, Clinton end logjam on Herman nomination.
newsitem.headline: Senate, Clinton end logjam on Herman nomination.

text.p: The Senate prepared to vote on President Clinton's nomination of Alexis Herman as labor secretary Wednesday moments after a deal was cut ending a dispute that had held up her confirmation vote.

Senate Deputy Republican leader Don Nickles of Oklahoma said the White House agreed to drop a planned executive order on federal construction projects as a part of the deal. Senate Republican leaders had objected to the order and held up the Herman confirmation vote until the dispute was resolved.
"I have been assured by White House officials that they will not issue this order, so I am keeping my pledge to release the Alexis Herman nomination," Nickles said in a statement.

The Clinton administration had planned to issue an order admonishing agencies to consider project labor agreements for federal construction. The agreements would set wages and terms of conditions of employment for union and non-union workers for the duration of each project.

Republicans, prodded by business groups, objected to the order, which they called a payoff to unions for their political support of Clinton and Democratic candidates that would discriminate against non-union workers and non-union contractors.

Instead, Nickles said, the administration will issue a memorandum to federal agencies reminding them that project labor agreements may legally be used if justified by time, cost and labor-management stability considerations.
